what: Several text frames are stacked on one stage pinned to the screen. Each frame gets its own scroll span in the document (default 100svh, 50~500svh via data-height) and is on only while passing through that span. It appears in the first 20% of the span and fades out over 15% starting at 85% (with cut, it switches right at the span’s start and end). Frames that are on get is-on, and the sum of the progress through each span’s middle (the second frame runs 0→2) is fired as fx:progress (detail.total) so the 3D scene camera behind follows it.

options.in: Length shown as a cell ratio, default .2
options.out: Fade-out length by cell ratio, default .15
options.at: Ratio of cells that start to disappear, default .85
options.[data-fx-part=frame]: Frame — data-height="200svh"(cell length), data-cut (switches immediately without a slide)
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Panel holding the frames (the element itself if none)

note: The original places the stage with position: fixed. This part does the same job with a sticky stage plus trailing cells, so it doesn’t break inside in-app scroll panels either

from.where: index.js frames on/off and frameProgress sum (#fps-root, 24 sections)
